chunks: Sadyr said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): What is incumbent upon the man in seeking livelihood?
He said: When you open your door and spread out your merchandise, you have fulfilled what is upon you.

key_terms.البساط: Bisat — the merchant's mat or display spread on which goods are laid out; by extension, the full spread of one's commercial activity
key_terms.الرزق: Rizq — divinely-apportioned sustenance or livelihood; in Islamic thought, God is the ultimate provider (al-Razzaq)
key_terms.قضيت ما عليك: You have fulfilled what is upon you — the completion of one's religious/moral obligation; emphasizes ease and removal of burden

ai.seo_question: What is a Muslim's obligation in seeking livelihood according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith, the companion Sadyr ibn Hakim asks Imam al-Sadiq (AS) about a person's religious obligation regarding earning a livelihood. The Imam's response is remarkably concise and liberating: the obligation is fulfilled merely by making oneself available — opening one's place of business and displaying one's goods. This teaching reflects the Imam's broader understanding that sustenance (rizq) ultimately comes from God, and the human duty is only to take the reasonable steps of availability and readiness, not to guarantee an outcome. The audience, 8th-century traders and craftsmen, would have understood 'opening the door and spreading the mat' as the standard idiom for beginning a day of commerce.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Abdul Rahman Bin Hammad, from Ziyad Al Qindy, from Al Husayn Al Sahhaf, from Sadeyr who said, 
‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Which thing is upon the man regarding seeking of the livelihood?’
So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If you open your door (of shop) and spread out (neatly) your merchandise, so you have fulfilled what is upon you’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from ‘ Abd al-Rahman ibn Hammad from Ziyad al- Qandiy from Al-Husayn al-Sahhaf from Sadir who has said the following: “This is concerning my question before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘What should a man do for work to make a living?’
He (the Imam) replied, ‘If you open your door and spread your merchandise, you then have done what should have been doing.’”
